note: Written and committed BEFORE any LV13 load-flow number was run. Do not edit after the first run without issuing a new revision and saying why.
question: Do the four operating cases of the 400 MW connection model solve with voltages and loadings inside limits, or are the exceptions explained?

voltage_limits_pu.basis: Author's design criteria. NOT SOURCED to a standard: no grid code or standard was read for this block. To be checked against the Grid Code and equipment specifications before any claim of compliance.

loading_limit_percent.basis: Loading is current over the provisional continuous rating (cables) or apparent power over the nameplate MVA (transformers). Cable ratings are PROVISIONAL and ASSUMED; they are replaced by the cable-sizing block (LV14).

pass_rule: A case is INSIDE LIMITS only if it converges and every bus voltage and every branch loading is inside the limits above. A bus or branch outside a limit is an EXCEPTION. Every exception is explained by a computed cause (a number from code). A remedy may be shown only as a separate, labelled what-if run; the base case and its limits are never changed after the run.
convergence: pandapower runpp, algorithm nr, init flat, tolerance_mva 1e-9, max_iteration 50, calculate_voltage_angles True, enforce_q_lims False.

bus voltage angle, pandapower vs independent solver

sum of generation minus power into the grid equals total branch loss

sensitivity on the two least certain inputs (grid short-circuit level 5 and 20 GVA against 10 GVA; export cable capacitance -20 and +20 percent). Reported as the change in the worst voltage and worst loading; an inside-limits verdict that flips is reported as sensitive.
export cable charging per circuit V^2*omega*C and full-load string current recomputed by hand-style formula, against model outputs
